concepts.def: The Sun, eight planets, moons, asteroids and comets.
Planets orbit the Sun in ellipses.
Gravity provides the centripetal force for orbits.
Icy bodies on highly elliptical orbits.
Rocky bodies, mostly between Mars and Jupiter.
Bodies like Pluto that don't clear their orbit.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Exploring the Solar System — a core area of GCSE Astronomy.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Exploring the Solar System brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Exploring the Solar System.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: How many planets are in the Solar System (IAU 2006)?
Who proposed the heliocentric model in 1543?
options: Galileo
Copernicus
Kepler
Ptolemy

mcqs.q: Why is Jupiter classified as a gas giant?
options: Its bulk is mostly hydrogen and helium with no defined solid surface.
It is made of fire.
Because clouds block them.
It is mostly air like Earth's atmosphere.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between a solar eclipse and a lunar eclipse?
options: Solar eclipses happen by day, lunar at night - that is the only difference.
Because clouds block them.
In a solar eclipse the Moon blocks the Sun; in a lunar eclipse Earth's shadow covers the Moon.
Lunar eclipses are more dangerous.

mcqs.q: Why don't we have a solar eclipse every new moon?
options: Because clouds block them.
Eclipses happen randomly.
The Moon's orbit is tilted, so it usually passes above or below the Sun's apparent position.
Lunar eclipses are more dangerous.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Heliocentric model”?
options: Average Earth-Sun distance, about 150 million km, used to measure Solar System distances.
G-type main-sequence star at the centre of the Solar System, containing 99.86% of its mass.
Body orbiting the Sun, massive enough to be spherical, that has cleared its orbital neighbourhood.
Sun-centred model of the Solar System established by Copernicus in 1543.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Sun”?
options: Like a planet but has not cleared its orbital neighbourhood; includes Pluto, Eris, Ceres.
G-type main-sequence star at the centre of the Solar System, containing 99.86% of its mass.
Average Earth-Sun distance, about 150 million km, used to measure Solar System distances.
The Sun and everything bound to it by gravity: 8 planets, dwarf planets, moons, asteroids and comets.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Planet (IAU 2006)”?
options: Average Earth-Sun distance, about 150 million km, used to measure Solar System distances.
Like a planet but has not cleared its orbital neighbourhood; includes Pluto, Eris, Ceres.
Body orbiting the Sun, massive enough to be spherical, that has cleared its orbital neighbourhood.
G-type main-sequence star at the centre of the Solar System, containing 99.86% of its mass.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Dwarf planet”?
options: Like a planet but has not cleared its orbital neighbourhood; includes Pluto, Eris, Ceres.
G-type main-sequence star at the centre of the Solar System, containing 99.86% of its mass.
Sun-centred model of the Solar System established by Copernicus in 1543.
Body orbiting the Sun, massive enough to be spherical, that has cleared its orbital neighbourhood.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Solar System”?
options: The Sun and everything bound to it by gravity: 8 planets, dwarf planets, moons, asteroids and comets.
Body orbiting the Sun, massive enough to be spherical, that has cleared its orbital neighbourhood.
Average Earth-Sun distance, about 150 million km, used to measure Solar System distances.
Sun-centred model of the Solar System established by Copernicus in 1543.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Astronomical Unit (AU)”?
options: Like a planet but has not cleared its orbital neighbourhood; includes Pluto, Eris, Ceres.
Body orbiting the Sun, massive enough to be spherical, that has cleared its orbital neighbourhood.
Average Earth-Sun distance, about 150 million km, used to measure Solar System distances.
The Sun and everything bound to it by gravity: 8 planets, dwarf planets, moons, asteroids and comets.

mcqs.q: Approximately how many million kilometres is 1 AU?
options: 225 million km
150 million km
75 million km
120 million km

numericals.q: Approximately how many million kilometres is 1 AU?

free_texts.q: Pluto was reclassified in 2006 as a what?
free_texts.hint: Two words - smaller than a regular planet.
